title: Velocity Cushion: headcount & price-slope playbook
content:
Overview:
This is a working budget + headcount workbook for Q3–Q4 2026 that ties a small set of pricing-sensitivity experiments to hiring phasing and an operational capacity cushion ("velocity cushion"). The doc is intentionally light on polish — meant to capture hypotheses, triggers and a minimal numeric model that product/ops/eng can iterate on.

Key goals:
- Produce a set of 'actionable triggers' that map price moves => hire / contractor swaps / burst-credit usage.
- Model three scenarios for token-price slope and token-velocity changes and show headcount delta + runway impact.
- Recommend a headcount phasing plan that keeps latency SLOs for Dedicated and Hosted tiers while preserving a 12–16 week cash cushion.

Assumptions (high-level):
- Baseline token price (per 1k effective tokens) = $0.018; compression scenarios to $0.012 and $0.009.
- Quantization adoption: incremental cost savings of 12–28% depending on model mix and GPU generation (NVIDIA H100 vs A100-ish).
- Burst credits available to ops equal to 15% of monthly commit capacity; cost per burst token assumed 1.4x baseline.
- Average engineer fully-loaded cost (incl benefits, bench) = $240k/year (SWE / ML-Infra level); contractor rate approximated at 1.6x equivalent for short-term work.

Scenarios (named):
1) Base-stable: token price holds; adoption of quantization at ~18% of requests by end-Q4; 6 net hires (eng/product) across two quarters.
2) Throughput-growth: token velocity +40% YoY (higher retention / new product launches); we need +18 hires to maintain latency SLO for Hosted; capacity-managed via Dedicated commits — revenue improves but unit-cost pressure increases.
3) Price-compression (adverse): unit price declines 40% from baseline; net revenue per token drops -> need to defer hires, accelerate quantization and routing policies, and rely on burst credits for peak.

Quarterly headcount phasing (quick matrix):
- Roles: infra-engineer, runtime-engineer, product-ops, sales-ops (support for estate onboarding), finance-analyst.
- Base-stable (Q3->Q4 2026): +2 infra, +1 runtime, +1 product-ops, +2 sales-ops = 6 hires phased as 2/4 each quarter.
- Throughput-growth: +10 infra, +4 runtime, +2 product-ops, +2 finance (18 total) — hire acceleration window 8–12 weeks.
- Price-compression: hiring freeze after Q3; convert 4 open reqs to contractors for 3–6 months, redeploy product-ops to pricing experiments.

Pricing sensitivity model (mini):
- Elasticities used: demand elasticity for tokens = -0.6 baseline (conservative), -0.9 for enterprise features; adoption elasticities differ by route.
- Unit margin = price_per_1k_tokens - marginal_inference_cost. Marginal cost modeled as GPU-hours converted to token-level cost with batching/quantization effects.
- Sensitivity outputs (toy numbers):
  * Baseline unit margin: $0.010 per 1k tokens.
  * Compression to $0.012 -> margin -> $0.004.
  * Compression to $0.009 -> margin negative (-$0.001).
- Trigger bands: if margin < $0.005 => activate hiring-slow protocol; if margin < $0.001 => immediate contractor-conversion + restrict burst.

Velocity cushion (operational reserve):
- Definition: capacity budget (in GPU-hours) equivalent to a 12% uplift over committed capacity to absorb token-velocity shocks for 6 weeks.
- Funding: paid from a short-term contingency bucket (3–6% of monthly burn) and prioritized over non-essential marketing spend in adverse months.
- Use rules: velocity cushion used only when 7-day token velocity > 110% of rolling-12w median AND margin still >= trigger threshold. Otherwise fallback to price-differential routing.

Actionable trigger map (week-level):
- Week 0–2 (early signal): 7d token velocity > +8% => Ops run auto-batcher adjustments and 24h KV-cache warmup; finance sends an alert to execs.
- Week 2–4: velocity persists and marginal margin compressed by >25% -> pause non-critical hiring (all reqs younger than 30d) and open contractor budget.
- Week 4+: persistent compression (4+ weeks) => enact hiring-freeze, prioritize quantization rollouts, shift traffic to cost-optimized model variants.

Cost/Runway sensitivity summary (example outputs):
- Base-stable + planned hires => runway reduction of 3.7 weeks vs no hires.
- Throughput-growth + hires funded by revenue => runway neutral (revenue grows offsetting cost) but cash timing lags (need 6 weeks of committed capacity financing).
- Price-compression scenario => runway shortfall estimated 8–11 weeks unless we implement 30% immediate opex cuts and 40% hiring deferral.

Open questions / risks (notes-to-self):
- Are we confident in the -0.6 elasticity assumption? Run an AB test on price-facing incentives for a targeted cohort.
- How quickly can Serving Runtime enable quantization for the 2 largest model families (LlamaX / Code models)? Engineering ETA needed.
- Legal implications for contract conversions (full-time to contractor) — payroll vs vendor classification risk. Loop legal.

TODOs (short list):
- [Finance] Build a variant of the token-level marginal cost sheet that includes per-model quantization delta (due 2026-05-21).
- [Eng] Cost-saver P0: prioritized list of 3 low-risk quantization rollouts (due 2026-05-28).
- [People Ops] Create contractor backlog & estimated ramp-down costs (due 2026-06-01).
- [GTM] Simulate commercial response to a modest price cut for SMB (internal scenario) — deliver impact to run rate and churn within 2 weeks.

Notes on modeling choices (internal rationale):
- Use a small number of discrete scenarios rather than a continuous monte-carlo for speed; finance-run MC still useful as follow-up.
- Prioritize metrics that product and infra teams own: tokens/route, 95th latency, marginal cost per 1k tokens after batch/kv/quantization.
- Keep burst credit as a safety lever — avoid overusing because of 1.4x marginal cost.

Appendix (quick numbers snapshot):
- Monthly baseline tokens (all routes): 18B tokens.
- Monthly revenue at baseline: ~$324k (back-of-envelope; internal details in linked sheet).
- Committed Dedicated capacity monthly cost equivalent: $1.1M (gross).
- Velocity cushion target GPU-hours: 3.4k GPU-hours/month (H100-equivalent).

References and links (quick):
- Confluence: FIN-pricing-playbook (internal id above)
- Jira: FIN-7821 (pricing-sensitivity experiment); FIN-7899 (quantization rollouts)
